title: Reduce GPU dependency footprint and build ABI compatibility harness for Triton/CUTLASS
creator: Asha Patel
description: Audit and shrink our GPU native dependency surface (CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS) and add a reproducible ABI/compatibility harness. Work includes removing unused linkage, consolidating multiple CUTLASS forks, adding a CI job to smoke-test ABI stability across CUDA/Triton matrix, and small performance cleanups triggered by the audit. Goal: reduce release risk from mid-stack updates and cut down image sizes and link-time failures seen after CUDA minor upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline artifact: reduce runtime native library size by >=8% in release image (measured by docker image diff)
CI job 'gpu-abi-matrix' green across CUDA 12.2/12.5/13.0 and Triton 2.x/3.x nightly targets
No new symbol collisions in runtime link step for both static and shared builds
At most 2% regression in end-to-end 512-token latency p95 on aml-gpu-test, or a documented mitigation plan
Documentation updated: dependency matrix and rollback steps added to CONTRIBUTING.md and release playbook
technical_notes: Current problem: multiple components link against different CUTLASS variants (internal shim + downstream vendored copy) causing ODR and symbol aliasing during LTO-enabled builds.
Proposed approach: introduce a single CUTLASS compatibility shim layer (thin adapter) compiled as a single shared object and referenced by all targets to avoid duplicate symbols.
We will replace ad-hoc -Wl,--allow-multiple-definition workarounds with explicit symbol visibility annotations and selective static linking where necessary.
Add a lightweight ABI checker that runs nm/objdump on built .so and compares exported symbols across matrix; fail CI on unexpected removals but warn on additions unless gated behind feature flags.

Performance cleanup: micro-optimizations in kernel loader path (avoid repeated std::regex in init; use single pass config parse), reduce memcpy in KV cache warmup, and remove stale vendor CUDA helper code paths not used by current models.
Risk: shim may mask behavioral changes; will add targeted integration tests (simple GEMM golden outputs) to ensure numeric parity for representative kernels.
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Spike completed; reproduced symbol collision locally with CUDA 13.0 + Triton3 and captured failing link logs (see link).
2025-02-14: Design review with infra and runtime teams. Decided on shared shim as lowest-risk path. Action: Liam to prototype shared object and Asha to draft CI matrix.
2025-02-18: Prototype shim compiles; landing PR will change build graph to stop vendoring CUTLASS into multiple targets. Preliminary image size improvement ~6% on dev build.
2025-02-21: Added basic ABI comparator script and a lightweight golden GEMM test. Tests run locally across CUDA 12.5 and 13.0 docker images.
2025-02-24: First CI job for gpu-abi-matrix added to feature branch; failing on Triton3 nightly due to symbol mismatch in triton_plugin. Investigating plugin version pinning.
2025-02-27: Mitigation plan drafted: pin Triton ABI in CI, add extra symbol aliasing for legacy plugin to shim. Plan reviewed by @Marisol Reyes (runtime) — OK to proceed.

benchmarks: Dev build (before): image size 1,120MB; p95 latency 87ms on aml-gpu-test (512 tokens)
Dev build (after prototype): image size 1,055MB; p95 latency 88ms (512 tokens)
Target: reduce image size by >=8% and keep p95 within +/-2%
testing_plan: Unit: run ABI comparator against all built .so artifacts (nm + sorted symbol diff)
Integration: run golden GEMM tests across CUDA 12.2/12.5/13.0 and Triton 2.x/3.x containers
E2E: run subset of smoke load tests on dedicated-dev capacity; verify p95 and error rates
Canary: deploy runtime-1.20 canary to 2% of traffic with automatic fallback on error-rate spike
rollout_plan: Merge shim + CI matrix once green
Cut runtime-1.20-canary image and validate internal teams for 72 hours
If stable, promote to staged release and coordinate release with infra team for CUDA driver compatibility window
Post-release: monitor gpu-abi-matrix CI for 2 weeks and open follow-up tickets for any plugin-specific fixes
risks: Numeric drift in a few edge-case kernels due to different CUTLASS code paths — mitigated by golden numeric tests
CI flakiness due to GPU driver / container inconsistencies — mitigated by pinning driver/toolkit in the matrix
Incompatible Triton plugin ABI changes requiring conditional shims — may increase maintenance burden
notes: Design feedback: PM wants clear rollback steps in release playbook before merge (added under acceptance criteria).
Ask from infra: consider keeping a pinned vendor CUTLASS snapshot for emergency rollbacks to avoid day-of-release surprises.
Follow-up: create ENG-34125 to document shared-shim support policy and maintenance ownership.
